description: Interbasin water transfers in the United States and Canada is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Md. Abu Bakar Siddik et al. Interbasin water transfers (IBTs) can have a significant impact on the environment, water availability, and economies within the basins importing and exporting water, as well as basins downstream of these water transfers. The lack of complete data identifying and describing IBTs inhibits understanding of the role IBTs play in supplying water for society, as well as their collective hydrologic impact. Coverage: several countries (US, CA); published in 2023. Formats: ZIP, Excel, Shapefile. The data are held in Consortium of Universities for the Advancement of Hydrologic Science, Inc and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 36744111 bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is This resource is shared under the Creative Commons Attribution CC BY., taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support water-network, drainage and hydraulic studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
